author: Juliet Salinas
developer_reply: Hi Juliet, in Todoist, recurring tasks are based on completions. This means that a task will only appear on its due date once the previous instance has been completed. If you create a task that repeats daily, it will only show up in the "Upcoming" view on the current day. Once you complete the task, it will then appear on the following day.

5. Tap back to save the change.

text: TODoist is a FANTASTIC app! It is one of the better apps that I have worked with in business, yet to be honest I first stumbled upon it by looking for a timer app that would interact / syncronize with Trello. It was then that I read that ToDoist DOES sync with many other apps, and that if I were using Pomodone (a pomodoro timer app), then all that I do in ToDoist would be readily synced into Pomodone, allowing me to not only schedule and prioritize my time but ALSO to discipline myself to accomplish it through timers. If you are using ToDoist than Pomodone seems like it was built purely to enable your productivity goals in ToDoist! Together, these apps are unbeatable! Having said all of this, ToDoist is alone ABSOLUTELY worth the time and money to learn and to purchase! I have used MANY different scheduling or GTD systems, and ToDoist is far and away the best that I have used! Do yourself a great favor and learn the keyboard shortcuts!! These are very powerful in action. The app’s ability to understand common language / phrasing is simply uncanny! REALLY WELL DONE!!! I highly recommend ToDoist. I mysefl committed to changing the system that I was already using, (largely because of the tie-in between ToDoist and Trello and Pomodone), and I can certify that it was WELL worth my investment of time!

The most frustrating thing so far is that adding a new task adds it to the BOTTOM of the list, NOT at the top. I NEVER want this behavior. Adding a task at the bottom of the list means the new thing is lost from view and I have to manually rearrange the list. On the web app, you can control where to add a new item by using Shift+A, but there is no preference to ALWAYS do this! There is also no way to do "Shift+A" (that I've found) on the Android app. You have to create a task, then manually move it to the top. Also, sorting by date either doesn't work, or sorts the wrong way, because the newest tasks are still at the bottom. I cannot believe that this is the default, behavior, and that it cannot be set in a USER PREFERENCE. I sooooo miss Wunderlist.

text: I suppose that if what you want is a full-featured to-do list application  with lots of options and capabilities, this would be a good app. But for me  it's overly complicated. I did the only thing I knew how to do and that was to edit this review.  So here are my additional comments about what I found to be overly complicated.    For instance, I couldn't figure out how to have entries without deadlines.  So I was constantly getting overdue task notices sent to my email in-box.  I wasn't interested in that.  So I wanted to figure out how to turn off the email notices, and couldn't figure that out.  So I then tried to figure out how to lengthen the deadlines.  When I clicked on something, I think it was Remove Deadlines, or something like that, all of my tasks disappeared.  I'm sure that with enough time and effort I could have figured all of this out.  But I did put a nominal amount of time into it.  I did not see that methods to change the configuration were intuitive so deleted the app from my phone.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Jerry, thanks for the details. A task is due today by default only if you add it from the "today" or "7 days" view, if you go to a project, it won't have a default date at all. You can disable email notifications in the Settings at todoist.com. If tasks' dates changed, they disappeared from the overdue section, but are still in your projects.

text:
In project view I cannot hide completed tasks and my projects stay 
cluttered with completed tasks. I really want to like this app and have it 
become my primary tool for getting things done but this is a huge flaw for 
my use. If you think about a physical pen and paper todo list, there's 
something satisfying about crossing a line through the item or checking a 
once-blank box, that isn't there in this app. I want to feel like I can 
clearly see what I have left to do for the day. I would really appreciate 
if completing tasks made the task significantly different (strikethrough or 
making the text of completed tasks more transparent). I want to see that 
I've completed something (for the day). I think another fun addition for 
the programmers would be visually rewarding recurring tasks being completed 
with a little fireworks display or a little cute puppy or something next to 
the task. Please consider these additions to the app as it would really 
improve my life. I will still use this app but I would love for the app to 
respond more to my little successes each day. Thank you!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Tyler, you can split big tasks into sub-tasks and when you complete them, they will indeed stay on the list, grayed-out until you complete their parent. We'll look into adding more rewarding effects in the future :)

I wanted to create a thing to do that occurred every 4 weeks on Sunday, but the phrasing to do so wasn't intuitive and once I figured it out, it would change it to "every Saturday" for some reason.   Also, when I assigned a parent task, it would put it under the parent and then also list it separately as it's own thing, making it look like I had twice as many things to do. Also, it kept reassigning parent tasks when I moved tasks and since there's no way to edit multiple tasks at once, I had to individually reassign the parent to each task. Overall, my experience with the app was incredibly frustrating.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Amanda, sorry to hear that. To create a task that recurs every 4 weeks starting Sunday, you just have to enter "every 4 weeks starting Sunday" or enter a specific date instead of "Sunday". text: It's not an all in one package, but to be honest nothing exists like that yet. And maybe everyone needs something different and a complete life management system is too difficult to make for more than one person. This tool will facilitate tracking and remembering the action items you have to do on a specific day or at a specific time and also the next action items you can do during any discretionary time you might have. I still use manilla folders and a labeler for projects support files that I need to give to people in person. I'm also not satisfied with managing any project information in this app, other than simple association to know what an action is for. And I track my "someday/maybe" items, "waiting for" items, and triggers elsewhere. But when used in an already working personal productivity system that is your own, this app is the bee's knees for managing simple physical actions. So despite all the negativity I just gave it, I use this app every single day and wouldn't use anything else. It makes sense, as most of what we do everyday are just a bunch of simple actions. I've only have success when I track one action for each project. Just a tip. That's why I manage projects elsewhere. Only the very next action for each project goes in todoist, for me.

text: I have tried most of the todo apps on the market, including toodledoo, nozbe, trello, jira, asana etc.     For me, todoist is the perfect combination of structure and flexibility for my use. Very east to implement gtd systems with projects and contexts. It works great on both android and web (it seems all functionality is in both places), and the premium version is affordable enough for home use.    Very easy to create hiearchies such as subproject and different projects for work and private, while at the same time being able to create queries and views across all folders.   Possible to perform searches for just the subprojects of a given project, so you can ask for all the next actions for just work or just home.   Very easy to share projects/lists with others.  Good reminder feature.  If I have to point at anything negative, it would the lack of recursive sharing, and the fact that there is no suggestion/tab-complete when defining folter queries. Took a bit of research to find the query syntax, but was easy once I found it.

Dgt GTD is great. The next iteration, Soda, might be awesome, but with Todoist I found the same simplicity and intuitive interface that I loved with GTasks, a very extensive package of functionality, total flexibility of how to make my own system, and it works across all platforms, with almost identical interface. I'm impressed. I'm still in the process of digging into it's core and moving my big amount of notes into Todoist, but it's already working way better for me than any other I've seen. I'm still on the free version, which I think is plenty for most users permanently. text: After going back and forth between Todoist and TickTick for the past year (TickTick being my main ToDo app for several years), I have finally settled on Todoist. Quite simply, Todoist is the better app. It just does more. In fact, the more I really get into it the more it seems to do. This and I do prefer Todoist's UI. I like the way it looks and it just seems to flow better. It does (for the most part) everything that I need it to do...and then some. I like the ability to create projects and sub-projects within sub-projects. While TickTick does offer a Project feature (called Folders), as well as sub-projects (called Lists), they do not allow sub-projects within sub-projects.  With Todoist I can choose a different color for each individual project. This is not currently an option with TickTick. I also like the ability to create subtasks. However, I am missing the ability to create checklists within a single task, which is a TickTick feature that I used regularly. I especially like (with TickTick) that I could (within a single task) add different times for individual items on checklist. After every item was checked, the task was set to repeat, along with the checklist. I'm not sure why Todoist doesn't offer this feature but I am hoping they will add it. Still, Todoist is packed with a multitude of features, some of which I am still discovering. To get the most out out of Todoist, I do recommend visiting their website, as well as watching YouTube tutorials by seasoned Todoist users. My new favorite thing is the ability to create filters. I also like the ability to create uncompletable tasks. Not to mention, I am making serious use of the label feature. Needless to say, I'm all in. I officially love Todoist!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: LeeAnn, you can create checklists with sub-tasks. In fact, you can even create a sub-project with regular recurring tasks which would work as a checklist :) Still, we'll look into improving this in the future.

text: I need to clarify my last review with an edit. Some functionality of the Windows 10 version of this app have gone away. The Windows 8 version worked perfectly, but when using the Windows 10 desktop version of Todoist, you can no longer search a task and then edit that task from the search results. Nor can you see or edit the reminder time once you have set it. If you have over a hundred tasks in your task list spanning 10 years as I do, this is an annoyance. Other versions of Todoist work well in these regards, including the Chrome extension and the smartphone app.  My work around it to go into the Chrome extension when I need to search and edit or check on a reminder. I wish Todoist would let you delete completed tasks.  They do not interfere with anything, and it is an intensional design feature so you don't ever loose tasks, according to the very responsive and helpful Todist support. Never the less, I find it annoying. Todoist support acknoledged the Windows 10 issue. All things considered, Todoist is still my favorite multi-platform task list program. The others multi platform task list apps don't come close. Yes, Wunderlist and Any.do, I mean you!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Donald, after performing a search you can just click on the task's name to edit it, this hasn't changed. If a task has a reminder, all you have to do is hover over the clock icon to see all details about all its reminders. Not being able to delete completed tasks ensures that you'll be able to find them later via search.

text: Here is a review after I used the app for over two years (one year free, one year paid, back to free now).  The app is great, definitely my favorite to-do app after trying out over 5 others, and having a bad time managing my time.   Free version highlights: - good minimalistic interface  - frequent updates - shortcut support  - custom natural language queries - smart re-scheduling based on AI algorithms  - priority sorting - good search for custom filters - nice karma point system for game junkies  Paid version highlights: - supports @tags - calendar syncing - custom filter support - good project support for multiple users  What I would love to have: - custom and more complex keyboard shortcuts - custom priorities + colors - more custom colors for projects (see Life Calendar colors for example, I want to have those) - have the calendar sync be a free option (just to get people in) - add some icons, like in Wunderlist - would like to have more graphs - (Web version) Add a button to move to a project when editing a task  Leaving it at 5 stars knowing the devs like to listen and we'll see updates eventually. Recommend it to any programmer,  and others.

text: Good app. A bit tricky at first, if you come from MS Outlook, for example. But once you get used to how it works, and how to program new todo's and reminders, it's very good.   For me, however, it lacks very important features. For example, let's imagine that ten notification reminders pop up in your cell phone at 8:00 a.m. For some reason, you have to restart your phone (e.g., it falls down and the battery slips off.) When you do so, your notifications are gone---and if they were a lot, you just won't remember which they were. Or, for example, let's imagine one notification pops up, and you take a look at the comment attached to it. After that, if you move to any other app or just return to home screen in your phone, notification is gone, even though you have not completed that todo.   There is no way to take a look at which todo's have notifications programmed for today (you can only see which todo's due dates are set for today.) Also it would be nice to have a way to take an easy look to a calendar when programming a reminder---currently you can only take a glimpse at a calendar when setting the due date.

text: This is the one! I've pretty much tried every task manager that's been out there but this is by far the best thing out there. Here are the highlights: APP SUPPORT:  Todoist supports EVERYTHING. I have a Mac, a PC, an android phone and an iPad and there are apps for all of them. And in the end up mostly using the web app because it's so good.  EASE OF ADDING TODOS:  You can add todos from anywhere, hotkey from any app in mac, the notifications screen in android, typing q in the web app, forwarding an email.  NATURAL LANGUAGE DATES/PROJECTS:  Todoist is even better than RTM. You can type, "Send weekly update every week on Friday #Work @office" and it will create a todo recurring every Friday in your Work list tagged with "office". Other apps force you to go to menus, drag things to the list you want and all sorts of horribleness. (I'm looking at you Wunderlist)  ADVANCED FEATURES: Too many to name. My faves: Set a time on a todo and it texts you a reminder, Space for project notes, unlimited comments on todos, photos added to todos, custom filters (Like todos for all my work projects due today).  Stop looking. Just get this.

text: Couldn't be happier.  Been using a number of Todo list apps on IOS, Android and PC for years and struggled to get one I was happy with; easy to use, seamless syncing across all my devices, nice interface and allowing me to group and arrange tasks as I wish.    Todoist has ticked the boxes.  It allows easy sorting, scheduling and grouping of tasks and basically does what it says on the tin very well.  Most importantly however it does so with a very slick interface that gets the trade-off between functionality and form just right.   The web interface is classy, as is the IOS interface.  The Android app (at least on my phone as opposed to my iPad)  is a bit more constrained but I suspect this is due to screen size limitations.  Finally, Todoist is well supported - there are maintenance updates to the web version occurring almost daily and a constant stream of new features.  So highly recommended.

text: Todoist is a pretty powerful app that can go a step beyond a to-do list, and it's particularly good for people who tend to work solo -  a lot of the other popular task lists/managers are really geared toward teams, and while that's great, I don't often work as part of a regular coordinated team, so a lot of the features of those other applications really don't apply to me.  I'd say that Todoist's best feature is the clean user interface. It's easy to read, easy to add tasks to (and the Chrome extension is very good for this) and lays out what you need to do for the week very nicely.  There are some cons, though. It's not obvious how to create subtasks and there's an extra step involved that I don't think is necessary. There are a couple of snags relating to repeating tasks. If you have a repeating task with subtasks, the subtasks are not "uncompleted" when the task refreshes (only the parent task is). If you have a repeating task that is overdue and you mark it as done, the current deadline is skipped and the task refreshes for the next one, which can throw you off a bit if you still have to  do the task for the current period.  All in all, it's a worth a try.

text: Todoist is not the most aesthetically attractive of the various task list apps out there, but for the most part, it is very functional. It's easy enough to quickly add tasks in the app, but I personally prefer adding things online or through the web app because it's much faster to type than it is to keep tapping keys on my phone.  What I like most about the app is that it is easily customizable. The app doesn't have any default categories to start you with; you are free to create "projects" viewable in the side bar as you wish, or none if that's more your style. This is the case for pretty much all of the other functions: they work, but if you don't feel like using them you don't have to.   If you like keeping a task list, at the end of the day it doesn't really matter which tools (digital or non-digital) you use to do it as long as you are effectively getting things done. Todoist is a great choice, but if you don't like the layout there are plenty of other options.

text: ToDoIst falls short of the GTD mantra in one key way: the focus is on setting labels, reminders, and projects at the time of task creation, and not IN BULK. With GTD you are supposed to dump all of your ideas into an inbox, then move each idea/task into smaller chunks with labels, reminders, projects IN BULK. This is to decrease the TIME and ENERGY it takes to create a workflow. With ToDoIst you have to INDIVIDUALLY edit each task's label, reminder, and project. This is a huge waste of time when you have 20 things in your inbox that need to be quickly sorted. It's, ironically, almost the complete opposite of the GTD mantra. All in all I think TDI is fantastic, but there really needs to be a "bulk" edit option to really take it to the next level. I understand that you can do this with due dates, but that's pretty much it. This needs to be applied to labels, reminders, and projects as well. If I need to quickly label 5 tasks as "y" and 8 tasks with reminders, I should not have to edit 13 different tasks independently.

text: The reason people use apps like these are not just to remember the things they have to do, but also to keep track of their progress, and inherently get a sense of reward when their tasks are finished. Of course, a completed task should be a reward in and of itself, but the ability to see your progress is very motivating. Unfortunately, ToDoist does not allow that - completed tasks disappear from their projects and the Today view, and are only visible with all the other historical completed tasks in a separate section of the app.  Users have been asking for this feature in a thread that's over a year old, and the company does not seem to think it is a priority.   I'm a premium user, and when my subscription ends I'll be moving on. In fact, if I find an app that does this and has the features of ToDoist, I'll leave, regardless of how much of my subscription I have used.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Andy, we're very sorry to hear that. If you have tasks that you want to see on your list after completion, you can use sub-tasks which stay there until their parent task is completed. You can of course also see them on the completed task list.

text: Todoist likes to pretend to be a free app, but to suggest that the free version is anything less than a trial is downright dishonest. Some pretty fundamental features, such as task reminders, are only available to premium users. What's worse, Todoist Free doesn't highlight which features are premium until you try to use them, meaning free users are constantly thwarted by popups asking them to spend money.  Rather than simply sell you the app, Todoist asks you to pay a sizable $29/year subscription fee, which in my view is a big downside compared to other similar apps.   All that griping set aside, I have to admit that it is a quality app. It's intuitive, simple, and highly customizable. I did a lot of shopping around an this is the only productivity app that does everything I want. I'm just hoping a cheaper alternative will emerge in the near future.

text: The app has a glaring bug: the calculation for daily repeating tasks breaks if you mark a daily task as complete after midnight. Instead of calculating one day from when the task is due, it calculates from when the task is marked done making the next due date tomorrow thus skipping today -- even though this is a daily task. This is a bug the developers know about and refuse to fix.  The location feature, like a few other features in this app, is incomplete.  It neither allows for the use of common locations (Home, Work, etc.), it also doesn't use Google's own starred locations. So, every time I want a reminder for when I arrive home, I have to enter the complete address (which autofills incorrectly).  Which renders this high-touted feature completely useless in practice. The app should either allow the selection of oft-used addresses from a list or use Google-starred addresses.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hello Joey. Sorry if recurring tasks doesn't fit your workflow... this is actually a design decision based on data, where most people find it more intuitive to base it on your current time. Also, Home/Work are not accessible, so we can't use them. Finally, you should be able to pick recent locations in 1 tap. If not, please reach out to us. Thanks!

text: If you just want some basic lists, ToDoist will do the job... that's where it ends. As a paid task list or to do manager. It fails on too many levels. Here are a few:  No Sorting: You cannot sort your tasks into due date order. This should be one of the most basic features of any task manager. You are required to use the 7 day view for this functionality, or the web version to order them. But as soon as you add a new task, it goes to the bottom regardless of due date.  Adding Task Dates: Adding due dates to tasks using terminology rather than the date picker is almost impossible. You need to write it in the exact format ToDoist specify, otherwise it won't work. If you want to see this functionality work well, check out Remember The Milk.  Reminders: Sometimes an automatic reminder will be set for a task, sometimes it won't. Even if it is set, it's hit or miss as to whether you will actually get it.  Sub-Tasks: You have to indent tasks to add sub-tasks. This is very unintuitive and means you'll often add sub-tasks in the wrong place.  Summary: Basically it's taken me more time to work around the ToDoist functionality than it's aided me as a task manager.

text: I paid for premium during the sale and now regret it. The app is quite sexy looking on the surface but has too many ui quirks to continue using it. So you have a list of tasks, some are subtasks, some are not. If you drag a regular task you'd expect it to behave the way a lot of apps do and drop it inside a subtask, but this doesn't work that way. Drag a task up into a subtask and it suddenly becomes the parent of that subtask and all the subtasks beneath it. How does that make any sense? When would I ever want to do that? Not to mention there's a long standing bug that when you go to edit a task and change the list it's in, it may or may not actually move. Right now I have two tasks that just live in the next 7 days view, and don't exsist in a list. I can automatically sort by date & priority, then I can quickly drag and drop to arrange tasks in a sequence that works for me. 3.  When I think of new tasks while driving, I can voice dictate new tasks using the Todoist Add Task Widget.  When I get to the office the new tasks are there written up in my task inbox. (voice dictation is dependent on other software.).  I'm a a child of the Franklin Planner in the 90's, but like element of the GTD system.  ToDoist is a perfect balance, allowing me to adapt it to my different context.  It is simple enough that it actually gets used.  It is adaptable enough that I want to use it. text: I love the android app, the minimalistic design and all its features. I even got the Chrome app extension since I go between my tablet and laptop a lot. It wasn't long until I came across the first bugs, involving the calendar. When I create a task on my laptop for Oct 31st, on my tablet it synchs as Nov 1st. When I go to change the date on my tablet, it doesn't work. When it does, the same task on my laptop doesn't reflect the change once synchronized. It gets really frustrating really quick. Why do all tasks I create on the website get bumped a day ahead on the android app? The timezones are the same on all platforms. Also, the sorting the tasks by date seems to work whenever it wants. I would really want to use ToDoist for both the personal and professional spectrums, I even wanted to go Premium, however its reliability right now worries me into avoiding it.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Roland, we're sorry to hear that. Based on past reports and our testing, the only way to trigger such behavior is having the time zone set differently that on Todoist and other devices you use it on. Even if your clock may be correct, if the zone isn't - tasks will be 1 day ahead. Please contact https://todoist.com/Support_Android/ for details.

text: Most of the others are toys, so far, but I've been using this for 2-3 years, before I got my Android tablet. I upgraded to the previous version, so I'd have more options. It gets better and better. I can now drag tasks from one project to another, color-code them according to priority, or type of task (something that I must do outside or several phases of the same task, for example). It's quite flexible and intuitive. It helps me avoid forgetting things, keeps me from feeling so overwhelmed by constantly thinking of things I need to or forgot to do (and because I can break things into small, manageable tasks), and I love clicking things off my to-do list. It also saves me time, because I enter labels by store or town, and then I can quickly sort them to group tasks together. It will send updates to email, but I access it on my office computer and my tablet, and it's great that I can do that both places and it's always in sync. No, nobody is paying me to write this rave review! I tried several similar apps, and this one's the best for me. And it even makes weekly productivity graphs for you! Perfect.
